name: Yellow-Green (Color Wheel)
lede: Yellow-Green (Color Wheel) is the standard hue that sits between [[yellow]] and [[green]] on a painter's twelve-step color wheel, qualified in our data to tell it apart from other lists' own Yellow-Green.

sections.title: A wheel position, qualified
sections.body:
The base name simply marks the hue's position on the color wheel, halfway between [[yellow]] and [[green]]; our data adds "(Color Wheel)" to separate it from [[yellow-green-crayola|Yellow-Green (Crayola)]], a different list's swatch for the same base name [1]. The xkcd 2010 crowd survey gives a brighter lime for a related submission, Leafy Green, measured about three units away [1].

Its closest measured look-alikes are [[kelly-green|Kelly Green]], read as almost the same color, and [[grass|Grass]], read as duller [1]. The ISCC-NBS 1955 system's nearest block is vivid yellowish green, about seven units from that block's center [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has this color covering at least one percent of its canvas, as photographed [2]. That describes this archive, not painting as a whole: a wheel-position swatch this saturated is rarer on an aged, varnished canvas than a muted historical green would be [2].
